title: People, body, temple (CCC 781–810)
hookLine: three images for what the Church is

lines: A POINTED ROOF AND A DOOR.
A PEOPLE, A BODY, A TEMPLE.
cards: What is a church? Ask a child to draw one and you'll probably get a building: a pointed roof, a door, a cross on top. That's fair; it's what the word means on a street sign.

But the Catechism doesn't draw a building first. It reaches for pictures, the way scripture does, and gathers them around three: a people, a body, and a temple. Each one shows something the others miss.

teach.b: Day three hundred eighteen met the body of Christ; today it's one picture of three. People first. God chose to make human beings holy not one by one, with no link between them, but as a people.
The Catechism begins that story with Israel, the people God chose and made a covenant with, and reads the Church as growing out of it.
The first letter of Peter says it to scattered believers, in the Douay-Rheims: "Who in time past were not a people: but are now the people of God." A people has a history, a memory, a road.
The Catechism lists what marks this one: you join by faith and baptism, its law is love, its mission is to be salt and light, and its destination is the kingdom. Body.
Paul writes to a quarrelsome church in Corinth: "Now you are the body of Christ, and members of member."

One thing made of very different parts; the eye can't tell the hand it has no need of it. Christ is the head, the Catechism says, and the members are joined to him and to each other; when one part suffers, all suffer.
A people can drift apart. A body can't, not without bleeding. Temple.
Paul again: "Know you not, that you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?"
Here the Catechism quotes Saint Augustine, echoing the lesson on body and soul: what the soul is to the human body, the Holy Spirit is to the body of Christ, the Church.
A people without a body becomes a crowd; a body without the Spirit, a corpse; a temple without a people, an empty building.

how: Catholics pray for the Church and for their parish in the prayers of the faithful at Mass, and speak of the Church as the people of God, the body of Christ and the temple of the Holy Spirit.

games.q: you're Paul, writing to a church in Corinth that's split into rival groups. what picture do you give them?
games.why: "Now you are the body of Christ, and members of member." different parts, one body, no part to spare.

practice: If you belong to a parish, see it from the back pew: the regulars, the family who's always late, the person at the door, the priest; if not, take the church nearest you and the people who walk into it on Sunday.
Let them be a people, a body, a house with someone home. If you pray, pray for them by name or by face; if you don't, wish them well, one by one.

wordCard.voice: People. The first of the Catechism's three pictures of the Church: God's people, made holy together. Today's word.

orig.note: the Greek word for "people" in 1 Peter 2:10, "now the people of God".

carryVoice: Your line: three pictures. A people, a body, a temple, each needing the others. See you tomorrow.
